biography.plain_text: Warren E. Halle is an American property developer who founded the Halle Companies in Silver Spring, Maryland. Starting with carpentry contracting in 1972, he expanded into homebuilding, land acquisition and large planned communities. His projects include Kingstowne in northern Virginia and Seven Oaks in Maryland, while he remains president of the privately held group.

long_biography.plain_text:
Kingstowne transformed Warren E. Halle's business from regional home construction into development at metropolitan scale. He formed a partnership to buy a large Fairfax County tract in 1985, negotiated rezoning and arranged acquisition financing before settlement. The resulting community combined thousands of homes with offices and retail, giving the Halle Companies a model for controlling land, construction and long-term place-making.

Halle's portfolio spread through Maryland, where projects such as Seven Oaks and Odenton Town Center made him a longstanding regional developer. His public profile has remained deliberately low, but his civic activity is visible through the Martha and Warren Halle Foundation. The family foundation has directed grants to children's, health, education and community organisations while Halle continued leading the Silver Spring business.

uncertainties.detail: The direct Associated Press interview links Warren Halle and the Martha Ann yacht while naming the Halle Companies. The source record's former Horizons III is the same vessel under a later name, and the exact middle-initial name is independently tied to the company by court and business records. This combination excludes same-surname founders such as Bruce and Claus Halle.

Broad Self-made is based on positive evidence that Halle founded the business as a carpentry contractor and expanded it into homebuilding and land development. His education, original capital and family economic background are not public, so independent-start and advantaged-start subtypes remain unsupported.

Dun & Bradstreet continues to list Halle as president and key principal, and current public-record aggregation links his entities and trust structures with regional property holdings. Those facts support current Real Estate and Founder classifications; no complete private balance sheet or current equity percentage is public.

No reliable full birth date, birthplace, secondary nationality or identity-secure personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website met the proposal threshold. The Halle Companies website was not proposed because it was inaccessible during research, although business records identify it as the official domain.
Exact-name, middle-initial, company and site:forbes.com/profile searches found no dedicated Warren E. Halle profile. No Forbes social link is proposed.

Property developer captures Halle's defining practiced role, while Residential development identifies the principal specialism evidenced by thousands of lots and homes. Mixed-use development was omitted to avoid overlapping tags based heavily on Kingstowne, and no new candidate was created.

The short biography is a 54-word founder and wealth-origin card. The long profile shares only Halle and property development, then adds the Kingstowne transaction mechanics, integrated operating model, low public profile and family grant-making. Both exclude yacht details, private addresses, current wealth estimates and disputed development incentives.
